# Salam

> Salam is a compiled, statically typed programming language whose keywords
> exist in English and Persian. It compiles to native code through an
> LLVM or C backend, to JavaScript for the browser, and ships a large standard
> library (over 150 importable packages) plus a self-hosted compiler written in
> Salam itself.

The fastest way for a model to work with Salam is the MCP server in
`tools/mcp`, hosted at `https://mcp.salamlang.ir/mcp`, which exposes the
compiler, the standard library and the language reference as tools. Look a
construct up with `salam_docs`, find std functions with `salam_stdlib_search`,
and call `salam_check` after every edit instead of guessing whether code
compiles.

The CLI uses subcommands: check the version with `salam version`.
`salam --version` does not exist and fails with `unknown command`.

A Persian program starts at `تابع ریشه:` and an English one at `func main:`.
`تابع اصلی` compiles as an ordinary function but leaves the program with no
entry point.

Packages from other people's repositories are added with `salam add`; every
standard library package ships with the compiler and needs no `salam add`.
There is no `salam publish`: a package is published by pushing a `vX.Y.Z` git
tag. Install the compiler with the one-line installer from the install page
(`install.sh` on Linux and macOS, `install.ps1` on Windows; the current release
is v0.6.2).

## Start here

- [Complete language reference](../../SKILL.md): the authoritative guide to
  syntax, types, generics, the std catalog, compiler rules, porting from
  other languages and Persian Salam.
- [Language guide for AI agents](AGENTS.md): syntax, the enforced declaration
  ordering rules, and the toolchain traps that silently produce wrong
  behaviour. Read this before writing any Salam.
- [Standard library index](stdlib-index.json): every importable `std` package
  mapped to its public declarations, generated from the source tree. Nested
  packages are keyed by the dotted name an import uses, e.g. `encoding.json`.
- [MCP server](../../tools/mcp/README.md): setup, tool reference, and the
  environment variables that scope it to a workspace.

## Documentation

- [Getting started](../GETTING_STARTED.md)
- [Package manager](../PACKAGES.md): `salam.toml`, `salam.lock`, `salam init`,
  `add`, `remove`, `update`, `deps`, `search`, `install`, version ranges
  (`@v1.2.0`, `^1.2`, `~1.2`, `>=1.2`, `@latest`), checksums and the registry
- [Desktop applications](../DESKTOP.md): the one `gui.webview` package
  (`import gui.webview`, Persian `رابط گرافیکی.نمایش وب`), `salam new --desktop`
  and `salam bundle`
- [Supported platforms](../PLATFORMS.md)
- [LLVM as the default backend](../LLVM_DEFAULT_BACKEND.md)
- [JavaScript backend](../JS_BACKEND.md)
- [Profiling](../PROFILING.md)
- [Layout DSL elements](../LAYOUT_ELEMENTS.md): every HTML element the
  `layout:` block knows, with English and Persian names and placement rules
- [Layout DSL schema](../LAYOUT_SCHEMA.md): how elements, attributes and
  value types are declared in `std/layout`, and how generators work

## On the websites

- Package manager guide: <https://salamlang.github.io/Salam/packages/> (English)
  and <https://www.salamlang.ir/packages/> (Persian).
- Every standard library package has a page at `/std/<slug>/`, and nearly all
  of them start with tutorials in sections named `#guide-...`, for example
  `/std/net/httpd/#guide-...`. The generated `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` of
  each site list every page and carry the full text.

## Source of truth

- `std/`: the standard library; every package is ordinary Salam source and is
  the authoritative reference for its own API.
- `tests/en`, `tests/fa`: the test corpus, and the largest body of
  known-good Salam in the repository.
- `compiler/`: the self-hosted compiler, written in Salam.
- `compiler/langpack.salam`: the English/Persian keyword tables.

- [Contributing](../../CONTRIBUTING.md)
